subject: Dedicated GPU contention – urgent action & exec engagement requested
messages:
From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@acme-pay.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Production errors and huge token queueing on our reserved pool (urgent)

Soojin —

We started seeing elevated 5xx error rates and a steadily increasing token queue on our dedicated pool around 08:50 PDT. Latency for inference requests spiked from ~120ms p95 to >2s, and a subset of requests began returning 500/502. This is affecting our live payment authorization flow.

We are on a reserved capacity contract (monthly commit) and were told reserved throughput would cover our peak traffic. Can you confirm what happened and provide an immediate mitigation? We're seeing retries and user impact.

Attached is a snippet of request IDs we captured; let me know if you need more. Please escalate to the team — this is impacting our revenue pathing.

—Tom
Tom Hayes | Head of Platform, Acme Pay
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@acme-pay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and huge token queueing on our reserved pool (urgent)

Tom — thanks for the heads up and the request IDs. We see the spike on our side (internal alerting lit up at 08:49 PDT).

Immediate steps being taken (short list):
- Moving a small percentage (~20%) of your traffic to an alternate compatible model variant to reduce KV-cache pressure and headroom.
- Temporarily increasing burst capacity on your reservation for the next 30 minutes while we stabilize (pending final approval).
- Collecting diagnostics — attaching the current snapshot.

I will keep you updated every 15 minutes. Sorry for the disruption; we’re treating this as a Sev2 -> Sev1 escalation until stabilized.

Attachments: diagnostic_snapshot_20270712.tar.gz

—Soojin
Soojin Lee | Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and huge token queueing on our reserved pool (internal)

Quick internal notes / ask: 
- Snapshot shows KV-cache growth and long tail eviction around 08:46–08:52. We suspect a hot prefix from a customer-side traffic pattern change (longer prompts / higher seq lengths).
- Aditya: can ops flip the canary routing now (route 20% to smaller-ctx variant) and disable batching aggressions for Acme for 30m?
- Soojin: please request urgent burst authorization from finance/exec for 1 hour (we should also prep a credits offer for Acme if they want to avoid outage impact).

Acceptable mitigation path: canary->throttle batching->burst allocation->postmortem + model/quantization recommendation.

—Marissa
VP, Customer Success
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:40:18 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and huge token queueing on our reserved pool (ops)

Marissa / Soojin — ops confirmed canary routing completed at 09:37. Batching aggression disabled for Acme routes. Memory pressure subsiding but p95 still elevated (~750ms). We are standing by to attach burst capacity; need exec sign-off for >30m.

I pushed a condensed diagnostics link to the incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1289 — it includes KV cache histograms and tail latency breakdown.

—Aditya
Senior SRE
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production errors and huge token queueing on our reserved pool — exec authorization request

Vivek — forwarding the incident. TL;DR: Acme Pay is seeing sustained token queueing and increased 5xx starting ~08:49. Ops mitigations (canary route, batching adjustments) are in place; p95 improved but still >600ms and some 5xx remain. We recommend temporary burst allocation (+40% reservation) for 1 hour to avoid continued user impact while we stabilize and perform a deeper postmortem.

Why this is urgent:
- Acme is a high-value reserved-customer (DEAL-4821). Their checkout path is sensitive to latency and errors.
- We observed a workload shape change (longer prompts) that increased per-request token work and caused KV-cache thrash on the pool.

Request: Approve 60 minutes of burst (estimate cost impact: ~$6k) and permission to offer a small one-time credit if Acme requests it. I can provide a short customer-facing summary within 20 minutes after approval.

—Soojin
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@acme-pay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and huge token queueing on our reserved pool (resolved -> follow up)

Tom — follow-up now that we have stabilized the flow. Summary: 
- Timeline: 08:49 PDT spike → canary routing + disable batching at 09:37 → burst allocation approved and applied 09:41 → p95 returned to ~140ms by 10:05.
- Root cause (initial): sudden increase in average sequence length for a small percentage of requests that caused KV-cache pressure and eviction storms on the dedicated pool.
- Immediate remediation: routed 20% of traffic to smaller-ctx model variant, disabled aggressive batching for Acme, and applied a temporary +40% burst allocation for 60 minutes.
- Next steps: full postmortem (infra+customer), model recommendations (quantization profile + prompt-length guardrails), and a proposed goodwill credit to Acme while we complete the RCA.

I've attached the diagnostics snapshot and the SLA window we used to calculate impact. Expect an exec-readout and postmortem draft in the next 24 hours. Sorry again for the impact — we appreciate your patience.

Attachments: diagnostic_snapshot_20270712.tar.gz, acme_sla_window.pdf

—Soojin
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
